items.title: Dick Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: And Phil Mead, his trombone slide hits the hat.

ctx.x: I’ve always insisted that the straw hats be worn. And it’s been, I think a boon to us because our publicity is very good. The pictures of us in the Alumni Review for example with the hats on are terrific, it’s a uniform thing. But lately I’m getting a lot of resistance to wearing the hats. And two sources. Gordy Bourns says, “When I wear the hat I can’t play the tuba, the tuba hits it.” And Phil Mead, his trombone slide hits the hat. And that is absolutely right, those are justifiable complaints. So what we’ll…

items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: now Dick Sherman has got me listening to George Brunies

ctx.x: I’m going to ask you about something you said, you said, “We didn’t play or listen to much traditional jazz.” So what is traditional jazz for you?

Well again as I said, I have trouble putting labels on things. Some of the real West Coast Turk Murphy kind of stuff, I guess I never particularly enjoyed that. And I’ve never had much opportunity to play it so maybe if I did I would. But as I say I’m getting more and more blurred as I begin to go back now. Now probably at the moment my two favorite trombonists, after for years being kind of fan of bop trombonists, I mean J.J. Johnson and Jimmy Cleveland were my heroes, and still are, and yet as I listen to…
Was the band an entity at Hamilton as well? It sounds like you went off campus to play a lot of your gigs.
